pin.note: The skills tree sha is the portable pin (it is recomputed from the files of a checkout); the archive digest is a second witness. The tag tarball is over 150 MB (265 MB of documentation screenshots) and is not the digest.

baseline.note: The bytes the 2026-07 review read, long called the v2.53.0 snapshot. They are main on 2026-07-15 (pyproject says 2.53.0, five days before the 2.54.0 bump) and differ from the v2.53.0 tag in 56 files. The local copy was a gitignored directory and is no longer the pin.

securityReport.note: Generated before upstream's 2026-10-01 refresh of every skill: the content hash of none of the 162 scanned entries equals the hash of the pinned directory, and 15 pinned skills are not in the report at all. It is context for the review, not the review.

policy.selection: Audited SAFE skills plus EviMed-rehabilitated gap fillers with bounded tools, provenance, dependency preflight, and fail-closed safety rules

wholePackTest.note: A figure from the 2026-07 review; the way it was obtained is not written down anywhere, so it is kept and not claimed.

wholePackSecurity.scope: per-skill findings of upstream's scan of 162 skills (scanner 2.1.0); 1 more high and 502 lower findings are cross-skill

upstreamReview.method: Static, for all skills: each counterpart directory of the pinned tree was compared with the bytes the 2026-07 review read (file lists, metadata versions, SKILL.md lines added and removed by Python's difflib.SequenceMatcher with autojunk off); the libraries and Python floors its scripts and tests declare were compared with the runtime image's pins (library names resolved against the pinned libraries, the pack's code never run); upstream's scan report was read. Dynamic, for the four refreshed skills only: upstream's own tests and the image's smoke chains were run in a throwaway CPython 3.11 environment built from the image's exact pins. Nothing else from the pack was executed.

classes.A: Adopting the v2.72.0 counterpart as documented needs nothing from the runtime image as it is: every library it imports is in the image at a compatible version (names resolved against the pinned libraries), or it is text or standard library only.
classes.A*: As A by static evidence, but upstream declares Python 3.12 or newer, or newer library pins, only as its own test interpreter; becomes A when upstream's suite passes on the image's pins.
classes.B: Needs extra wheels beside the pinned stack that install on CPython 3.11 (named in the reason); nothing pinned moves.
classes.C: A pinned library must move, or the blocker is not a library at all (network egress, credentials, native executables, GPU).
classes.D: A core dependency, as pinned upstream, needs Python 3.12 or newer; blocked until the runtime interpreter moves.

decisions.refreshed: The skill carries upstream bytes: the whole counterpart directory was taken at the pin and the recorded edits applied.
decisions.held: The shipped directory is EviMed-authored (SKILL.md, agents/openai.yaml, executed by _runtime/execute_skill.py) and is unchanged; this row records the review of the counterpart(s), the class says what refreshing toward them would cost.

edits.E1: The trailing 'Citing Scientific Agent Skills' section is removed (it tells the agent to put the publisher's paper into the user's manuscript or report and to fetch a web page).
edits.E2: The compatibility line (upstream's tested environment) is replaced by one that is true of the runtime image.
edits.E3: No run-time install lines (uv add, uv pip install, uv venv, uv run --isolated --with): the runtime has no package registry; they become the image's interpreter or a sentence saying what the image carries.
edits.E5: Upstream's own --no-show flag is kept instead of EviMed's earlier plt.show() patch, and the image's office-smoke passes it.
edits.E6: EviMed's own additions are kept: the deterministic-baseline section, the export_power_analysis.py line and script.
edits.E8: Upstream's block-style metadata with last-reviewed is kept.

methodDependencies.$comment: Software a skill's full method needs that the runtime image does not carry, as the skill's own text names it, listed under the skill's name as { kind, name, optional?, mention, evidence }. The shared baseline above runs without it; a skill whose own instructions say 'check RDKit' or whose script exits without gseapy is not runnable for that method on an image that lacks the package, and the availability label says so. Empty since 2026-10-12: the image's python-methods phase (deploy/runtime-dsh/install-runtime.sh) installs rdkit, biopython, gseapy, scanpy, anndata and lifelines, which were the five entries this list held. Each entry quotes the mention that justifies it (checked against the skill's files by test/skillPackages.test.mjs); a name no skill text mentions is not declared here.
